TypeScript parser: a strict superset layer over the JavaScript handlers.

tsHandlers calls js.jsHandlers first, then registers the eight ts.yaml statements JS lacks (type_alias, interface, enum, namespace, module, declare, abstract_class, using) and overrides the handlers whose syntax TypeScript extends: declarator (type annotations are full types, ! definite assignment, const enum), function (angle-bracket generics, typed params, overloads without a body), class (generics, implements, decorators, accessibility and variance modifiers, parameter properties, index signatures), import / export (type modifier, export =, import =) and async_function (typed and generic arrows).

Types are parsed by a dedicated recursive-descent chain (parseTSType and friends) rather than the Pratt loop, so </> nest as generics instead of comparisons and as/satisfies take a type rhs (via the infix:as / infix:satisfies expression hooks). Value positions that stay ambiguous (f<T>(x) vs a < b) use speculative parsing with markLexer / restoreLexer: a generic call commits only when type arguments parse cleanly and a call paren follows, otherwise the default comparison path runs untouched.

AST shapes (all node kinds already exist in ast.nim):

  • Foo<Bar, Baz> reference: nkBracketExpr [base, args...]
  • unions/intersections: nkInfix [| or &, lhs, rhs] (engine order)
  • T extends U ? A : B: nkCall [conditional-type, T, U, A, B]
  • (x: T) => R: nkFunction [function-type, params, return]
  • new (x: T) => R: nkFunction [construct, params, return]
  • object types / interface bodies: nkBlock of member statements
  • property: nkStatement [property, readonly?, key, type]
  • method (type level): nkStatement [method, key, fn]
  • index signature: nkStatement [index, nkIdentDefs[name, keyType], valueType]
  • call/construct signature: nkStatement [call | construct, params, return]
  • mapped type: nkStatement [mapped, constraint, valueType]
  • tuple: nkArrayLit (...T is nkCall [spread, T], l: T is nkColonExpr, T? is nkPostfix [T, ?])
  • optional ? / definite ! on names: nkPostfix [name, ? | !]
  • type alias: nkStatement [type, name, genericsOrEmpty, aliased]
  • interface: nkInterface [name, genericsOrEmpty, extendsStmtOrEmpty, body]
  • enum: nkStatement [enum, name, body], members are nkIdentDefs [name, empty, initOrEmpty]
  • namespace/module: nkStatement [namespace | module, name, bodyOrEmpty]
  • declare: nkStatement [declare, decl]
  • abstract class: nkStatement [abstract, classNode]
  • using: nkStatement [using, nkIdentDefs [name, typeOrEmpty, init]]
  • decorator: nkPrefix [@, dec]; decorated decls: nkPragmaBlock [nkBlock(decs), decl]
  • import type / export type (braced/star): trailing nkIdent("type")
  • angle assertion <T>x: nkCast [type, operand]; .tsx never takes this path (see the < prefix handler).
  • function declarations mirror js.registerFunction's seven slots [keyword, star, name, generics, params, return, body]; methods are nkColonExpr [key, nkFunction(flags..., generics, params, return, body)]; fields are nkStatement [field, flags..., key, typeOrEmpty, initOrEmpty].
  • generic arrows: nkFunction [generics, params, returnOrEmpty, body]; async arrows: nkFunction [async, genericsOrEmpty, params, returnOrEmpty, body].
  • x as T / x satisfies T: nkInfix [as | satisfies, x, T].
  • a?.b / x!: engine default nkInfix [?., a, b] / nkPostfix [x, !].

Known limitations (documented, not bugs): JSX elements are not parsed — .tsx only disables angle assertions; full JSX grammar is a separate chunk. Angle assertions accept a reference type (<Foo<Bar>>x), not an arbitrary type (<(A | B)>x needs as). >>/>>> splitting covers generic nesting; >= never appears in type position.
